4. Posting Plan Output as a PR Comment
blocks.text: 4. Posting Plan Output as a PR Comment

blocks.content: Posting real plan output directly as a real, visible PR comment is a real, common, and genuinely valuable, practical pattern many real teams adopt.
This makes a proposed, real, infrastructure change genuinely visible directly within the same, real code review a team already does for application code.
Several real, existing GitHub Actions and Jenkins plugins automate this exact, real pattern, worth adopting rather than building it manually.
This connects directly back to the general, real principle of making changes genuinely visible before they merge, already emphasized throughout this course.
A real, updated comment, replacing the previous one on each new, real push, keeps a pull request genuinely clean, rather than accumulating repeated, real comments.
This small, real, practical detail makes the pattern genuinely pleasant to actually use, day to day, across a real, active team.

blocks.content: 5. A Real, Complete Example
Bringing this topic together, a real, complete plan stage runs on every PR, saves its output with -out, and posts a real, visible summary as a PR comment.
This is worth treating as a genuine, real starting template, adaptable directly to either GitHub Actions or Jenkins, covered in the two previous topics.
Every practice covered in this topic individually comes together here, into one, coherent, real, reviewable pipeline stage.
This exact stage is precisely what the Apply Stage topic, immediately ahead, depends on directly, completing the real, connected pipeline.

jobs:
  plan:
    steps:
      - run: terraform plan -out=tfplan
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: tfplan
          path: tfplan

blocks.content: 7. Recap: plan Is Genuinely Read-Only
Recall from the CLI module, plan is genuinely read-only, it never actually modifies real, live infrastructure, only computing and displaying a proposed change.
This is precisely why running plan on every, single real pull request is genuinely safe, with zero, real risk to actual, live infrastructure.
This honest, important distinction is worth recapping directly here, it is exactly what makes the practice covered throughout this topic genuinely safe to adopt.
This connects directly back to the real, honest safety already established for plan throughout the CLI module.
This genuine safety is precisely why a plan stage requires no real, human approval gate, unlike the apply stage, covered in the next topic.
This distinction, safe to automate versus requiring real, deliberate approval, is worth holding onto clearly through the rest of this module.

blocks.content: 8. A Real, Common Mistake
Running apply directly on every real pull request, rather than only plan, is a real, common, genuinely risky mistake, especially early in CI adoption.
This genuinely allows unreviewed, real changes to actually modify live infrastructure, directly from any real, proposed, unmerged pull request.
The honest fix is exactly the pattern covered throughout this topic, plan on every PR, apply only after a real merge, covered in the next topic.
This mistake is worth catching immediately during any real, initial CI pipeline setup, before it ever becomes a genuine, live habit.
